lessons.title: 3.6 Jihad: meaning, the greater and lesser jihad and the conditions for lesser jihad (Qur'an 49:15)
lessons.bigQuestion: The word 'jihad' is often misunderstood. What do you think its basic meaning is?
objectives: To understand the meaning of jihad, the difference between greater and lesser jihad and the strict conditions for lesser jihad
successCriteria: All: define jihad and the greater and lesser jihad
Most: explain the set passage 49:15
Some: explain the conditions for lesser jihad using 2:190-194 and 22:39
lessons.crossCurricular: History and citizenship: rules of war, from Islamic teaching to modern international law
lessons.smsc: Moral: struggle against wrongdoing in oneself; the sanctity of innocent life

keywords.def: striving or struggling in the way of Allah
the struggle against one's own self and sins
armed struggle in defence, under strict conditions
one who strives in the way of Allah

hook.text: The word 'jihad' is often misunderstood. What do you think its basic meaning is?
hook.a: Striving or struggling in the way of Allah: mostly against one's own self, and only in strict conditions in armed defence.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then do not doubt, and strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is they who are the truthful' (al-Hujurat 49:15). This is the set passage for 3.6.

starter.q: Name the four Sunni sources of Shari'ah.
Which ayah praises those who followed the Prophet ﷺ in the hour of hardship?

teach.heading: What jihad means
bullets: From j-h-d: to strive, to make effort
Set passage 49:15: strive with wealth and lives
Striving: worship, learning, da'wah, self-control
'Those who strive for Us, We will guide' (29:69)
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Portal lessons y11 25 and 26 are independent study. Read 49:15 and draw out: true belief shows in effort and sacrifice.

teach.heading: Greater and lesser jihad
teach.note: The spec uses these terms. A well-known saying about returning 'from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad' has a weak chain; scholars teach the struggle against the self from authentic texts, e.g. 'the mujahid is the one who strives against his own self for the obedience of Allah' (at-Tirmidhi).

left.title: Greater jihad
points: Daily: prayer on time, honesty, patience

teach.heading: Conditions for lesser jihad
bullets: Defence against attack or oppression (22:39)
Fight only those who fight you; do not transgress (2:190)
Stop when the enemy stops (2:192-193)
No harm to non-combatants, crops or places of worship
teach.note: 22:39: permission given to those fought against because they were wronged. 2:190-194 set limits. Abu Bakr's instructions to his army forbade killing women, children and the elderly and cutting fruit trees (reported in the Muwatta' of Malik). Declared by a legitimate authority, as a last resort, proportionate.

check.q: Which is NOT a condition of lesser jihad?
options: Fighting only those who fight you
check.why: Targeting civilians is forbidden: 2:190 forbids transgression; 5:32 makes killing one innocent like killing all. The others are conditions.

teach.heading: Misuse and the truth
bullets: Killing one innocent is like killing all (5:32)
Terrorism breaks every condition
Muslim scholars worldwide condemn it
Most jihad is quiet and personal
teach.note: Handle sensitively; pupils may face questions from others. Equip them with accurate, calm answers.

practice.q: Explain the difference between greater and lesser jihad.
practice.a: Greater: the lifelong struggle against one's own self to obey Allah (e.g. prayer, honesty). Lesser: armed defence under strict conditions (22:39, 2:190). Greater is for every Muslim always; lesser is rare and regulated.
practice.model: I do: 'Greater jihad is the inner struggle against one's own nafs to obey Allah, for example waking for fajr. Lesser jihad is armed struggle, permitted only in defence and under strict conditions such as 2:190 ...'

practice.q: Which ayah gives permission to those who were wronged?

independent.q: In the portal response box: a) set-passage answer: 'Explain what 49:15 teaches about jihad.' b) 12-mark plan: 'The greater jihad is more important than the lesser jihad.' Assess this statement.
independent.a: a) True belief is shown by striving with wealth and life; sincerity without doubt. b) For: daily, for all, character. Against: defending the oppressed is a duty when conditions are met; both are worship. Conclusion.
independent.model: Teacher models a): 'Qur'an 49:15 teaches that true believers do not doubt and strive with their wealth and lives in Allah's cause. This shows that jihad is ...'

independent.q: Extend: list four conditions for lesser jihad.
independent.a: Defensive or against oppression; legitimate authority; non-combatants protected; stop when the enemy stops; proportionate; last resort.

exit.q: What does jihad literally mean?
Back to our ponder: what is the basic meaning of jihad?
exit.a: Striving in the way of Allah, mostly against one's own self.

lessons.bigQuestion: Is a festival mainly about celebrating, or about worship? Can it be both?
objectives: To understand the origins, activities and significance of Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Adha and Ashura
successCriteria: All: describe the origin and main activities of each festival
Most: explain the set passage hadith on the two Eid days
Some: explain how Sunni and Shia Muslims mark Ashura differently
lessons.smsc: Cultural: shared celebrations of the worldwide ummah

keywords.def: the festival at the end of Ramadan
the festival of sacrifice on 10 Dhul Hijjah
charity paid before the Eid-ul-Fitr prayer
the sacrifice of an animal at Eid-ul-Adha

hook.text: Is a festival mainly about celebrating, or about worship? Can it be both?
hook.a: In Islam the two Eids are worship and celebration together: prayer, takbir, charity, family and gratitude.

islamicLink.text: Allah says of the sacrifice: 'Neither their meat nor their blood reaches Allah, but what reaches Him is taqwa from you' (al-Hajj 22:37).

starter.q: Which ayah: 'fight those who fight you, but do not transgress'?

starter.a: The struggle against one's own self
options: The struggle against one's own self

teach.heading: Set passage: the hadith of Abu 'Ubaid
bullets: Abu 'Ubaid prayed Eid with Umar ibn al-Khattab
Umar: the Prophet ﷺ forbade fasting on two days
The day you end your fast (Eid-ul-Fitr)
The day you eat from your sacrifices (Eid-ul-Adha)
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. The hadith is in Bukhari and Muslim. Portal lessons y11 27 and 28 are independent study. It shows the two Eids are set by the Sunnah, are days of eating and joy, and that fasting on them is forbidden.

teach.heading: The two Eids
teach.note: Eid-ul-Adha links to Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son and Allah's ransom (37:102-107). Qurbani meat is commonly shared between family, friends and the poor.

head: Feature
Eid-ul-Fitr
Eid-ul-Adha
rows: Takbir from the days of Dhul Hijjah
Eid prayer, takbir, new clothes, family

teach.heading: Ashura (10 Muharram)
bullets: Sunni: the Prophet ﷺ fasted it; Musa was saved
Fasting the 9th and 10th recommended (Muslim)
Shia: mourning Husayn's martyrdom at Karbala (61 AH)
Majalis, recitations and charity
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ found the Jews of Madinah fasting it for Musa's rescue and said 'we are closer to Musa than you' (Bukhari and Muslim). Fasting it expiates the previous year (Muslim). Husayn ibn Ali was killed at Karbala in 680 CE; Sunni Muslims also honour Husayn. Teach the Shia practice factually and respectfully.

check.q: Why do Sunni Muslims fast on Ashura?
options: The Prophet ﷺ fasted it to mark Musa's rescue
check.why: Bukhari and Muslim: he fasted it and recommended it, connected with Musa. Mourning Husayn is the main Shia focus; it is not the end of Ramadan or start of Hajj.

teach.heading: Significance today
bullets: Unity: the whole ummah celebrates together
Charity: no one left out
Gratitude and remembrance of Allah
Identity for Muslims in Britain
teach.note: 12-mark statement: 'Eid-ul-Fitr is more important than Eid-ul-Adha.' Assess this statement. Sample assessment material Question 6(c) and 6(d).

practice.q: Explain what the hadith of Abu 'Ubaid teaches about the two Eids.
practice.a: They are the two festivals set by the Prophet ﷺ; fasting on them is forbidden; they are days of eating, joy and gratitude linked to Ramadan and the sacrifice.
practice.model: I do: 'The hadith teaches that the Prophet ﷺ forbade fasting on the two Eid days. This shows that Eid is a day of celebration and gratitude, after worship ...'

practice.q: When is zakat al-fitr paid?
practice.a: Before the Eid-ul-Fitr prayer

independent.q: 12-mark answer in the portal response box (or Forms long answer): 'Eid-ul-Fitr is more important than Eid-ul-Adha.' Assess this statement.
independent.a: For: ends Ramadan, zakat al-fitr, gratitude for the Qur'an's month. Against: Eid-ul-Adha linked to Hajj and Ibrahim's sacrifice, called 'greater Eid' by many; the hadith pairs them equally. Justified conclusion.
independent.model: Teacher models the 'against' opening: 'Others would disagree, because Eid-ul-Adha remembers Ibrahim's complete submission to Allah (37:102-107) and comes with Hajj ...'

independent.q: Extend: compare how Sunni and Shia Muslims mark Ashura.
independent.a: Sunni: fasting the 9th and 10th, remembering Musa. Shia: mourning Husayn's martyrdom at Karbala with gatherings and recitations.

exit.q: On what date is Eid-ul-Adha?
Back to our ponder: celebration or worship?
exit.a: Both: prayer, takbir and charity with family joy.

keywords.def: the marriage gift that belongs to the bride
the sacrifice and celebration for a newborn

hook.text: What makes a family strong? What does a child owe their parents, and what do parents owe their child?
hook.a: Love, mercy and tranquillity (30:21); kindness to parents (46:15); care, education and a good name for children.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates so that you may find tranquillity in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy' (ar-Rum 30:21).

starter.q: Who narrated the set passage on the two Eid days?
What do Shia Muslims commemorate on Ashura?
starter.a: The martyrdom of Husayn at Karbala

starter.q: Which ayah: 'neither their meat nor their blood reaches Allah'?

teach.heading: Marriage in Islam
bullets: A Sunnah of the prophets and a contract (nikah)
Consent of both is required (Bukhari and Muslim)
Mahr belongs to the bride (4:4)
Witnesses; a wali for the bride (majority of scholars)
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Portal lessons y11 29 and 30 are independent study. The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever turns away from his Sunnah is not from him, in a hadith that includes marriage (Bukhari and Muslim). In Britain, Muslims also register the marriage under British law. Keep to the spec; no relationships education content.

teach.heading: Set passages: 30:21 and 46:15-18
bullets: 30:21: tranquillity, affection and mercy are signs of Allah
46:15: kindness to parents; the mother's hardship

lessons.unit: Summer 1: Final preparation
lessons.title: Optional clinic before the exam (Mon 24 May)
lessons.bigQuestion: What is the one question you would most like answered before Wednesday?
objectives: To understand and fix the last questions I have before the 4IS1 paper on Wednesday
successCriteria: All: bring and resolve one question
Most: rehearse one 12-mark plan aloud
Some: help a classmate with a topic I know well
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: calm and reliance on Allah

keywords.def: a drop-in session to fix specific questions
practise saying or doing something before the real time

hook.text: What is the one question you would most like answered before Wednesday?
hook.a: Pupils' own: bring it to the clinic.

islamicLink.text: Musa (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام) said: 'My Lord, expand for me my chest and ease for me my task' (Ta Ha 20:25-26).

starter.q: How many questions do you answer?
Which set passage are you least sure of?

teach.heading: How the clinic works
bullets: Post your question in the chat
Teacher groups similar questions
Breakouts for A, B and C
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Optional session (TO CONFIRM attendance). No new content.

teach.heading: Rehearse a 12-mark plan
teach.note: Model aloud, then pupils do one.

model.problem: 'The Day of Judgement is the most important belief.' Plan aloud.
steps: For: it gives life meaning; deeds weighed (101:6-9)
Against: tawhid is the foundation (112:1-4)
Against: all six articles are required
Judgement: tawhid first; Akhirah gives urgency
model.answer: A balanced plan in two minutes

teach.heading: Calm before the exam
bullets: Prepare, then rely on Allah
Sleep, Fajr, breakfast
A du'a from the Qur'an: 'My Lord, expand my chest'
teach.note: Ta Ha 20:25-26: 'My Lord, expand for me my chest and ease for me my task.'

practice.q: Say a 12-mark plan aloud for a statement from your weakest section.
practice.a: A balanced plan with a passage and a judgement
practice.model: Teacher plans 'Salah is more important than Hajj' aloud in two minutes: for, against, passage, judgement.

practice.q: What will you do the night before the exam?
practice.a: Light review, salah, sleep

independent.q: Clinic breakouts: work on your chosen question with the teacher or the section group; then write one improved answer in the portal response box.
independent.a: One improved answer on the pupil's own question
independent.model: Teacher answers the most common question first for everyone, then opens breakouts.

independent.q: Extend: test a partner on five set passages.
independent.a: Pupils' own

exit.q: Write your one-line exam-day plan.

lessons.homework: Rest, light review of set passages, and du'a. There are no live Islamic Studies lessons after the exam. Exam: 4IS1 Paper 1, Wed 26 May 2027 (morning), 2 hours 30 minutes, 90 marks.
